title: Rules that are not per kind
description: Two sets. The **cross-kind conditionals** hold of a node whatever its kind and cannot sit in one of the eight files without being written eight times. The **cross-node rules** need to see more than one node at once, so no per-file schema can express any of them and a validator over the whole network is the only place they can be decided.

gap_alternation.rule: A node declares everything its kind requires, or declares a gap naming what it lacks.
gap_alternation.shape: anyOf: [ every field the kind requires, gaps ]
gap_alternation.weakness: `gaps` there is any gap over any field, so a gap about one fact would otherwise excuse the absence of another. Both directions are held by the network validator, not by the schema.

modeled_needs_rationale.rule: A node whose `origin` is `modeled` carries `rationale`, or a gap.
modeled_needs_rationale.why: A reviewer accepts a fact the material stated and disagrees with one the analysis reached, and can do the second only against a reason.

authoring_gap_excuses_three.rule: A node with no open `kind: authoring` gap declares `question`, `description` and `out_of_scope`.
authoring_gap_excuses_three.why: An open authoring gap is what says a pass has not run, which is why there is no status field and none to forget.
authoring_gap_excuses_three.coarse: Any authoring gap excuses all three; which field each gap owes is decided by the completeness check, where a per-field answer can be given.

scope_has_no_boundary.why: A scope belongs to no scope. Its absence is what identifies a partition root.

kind_is_the_construct.why: The kind is the construct here, so a `ddd` beside it would name the same fact twice.

identifier_arithmetic.rule: Every identifier computes to the path it sits at, and the kind in the identifier agrees with the kind the node declares.

gaps_and_absences_agree.rule: Every gap names a fact the kind requires and the node lacks, and every fact it lacks is named by a gap.

lifecycle_totality.rule: For every pairing of a declared state with a trigger the table mentions, either a transition or a rejection exists.

one_lifecycle_per_subject.rule: No two lifecycles name one definition as subject.

crossing_targets_an_interface.rule: A reference whose origin and target sit in different bounded contexts targets an `interface`.

references_resolve.rule: An edge naming an identifier the network does not hold is reported as a defect, never repaired.

x-owed.state_reachability: Every state is reachable from `initial`, and every non-terminal state has an outgoing transition. Specified; no shipped script decides it.
x-owed.cycles: A cycle is reported together with unresolved edges and orphans. Specified; no shipped script decides it.
x-owed.cardinality: Every edge's cardinality is enforced. Declared in tables/edges.json; only `lifecycle.subject`'s inverse bound is decided anywhere, and by hand.
x-owed.orphans: An orphan is reported. The materializer's rule counts a node as referenced when it is the *source* of any edge, and every node but a scope declares a `boundary` — so for six of the eight kinds the rule cannot fire. A semantically isolated node is not the same thing as an orphan, and nothing decides the first.
x-owed.boundary_validation: A node is validated against the frontmatter contract at the boundary. Specified; the distribution ships no validator that does it, and the record and result contracts are checked by model judgment rather than by a script.
x-owed.body_form: One sentence per line, exactly one RFC 2119 keyword, the two headings the kind names, and the body-length ceiling. Specified; nothing decides any of the four.
